newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo to lose more industrial jobs in 97-Fiesp.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo to lose more industrial jobs in 97-Fiesp.

text.p: Industrial jobs in Sao Paulo will continue to fall in 1997 as companies restructure to become more competitive, said an official at Sao Paulo's Industries Federation (Fiesp).
"In 1997, we see job levels remaining negative or possibly stable if enough new plants come on line this year," said Horacio Lafer Piva, head of Fiesp's research department.

In 1996, Sao Paulo state industries sacked 176,142 workers, or 8.17 percent of the state's workforce. Since the Brazil launched its anti-inflation Real Plan in July 1994, industry has laid off 320,864 workers as it modernizes to adjust to greater economic opening, Fiesp said.

Brazil will only see industrial job growth in 1997 if the economy grows between five percent and six percent, Piva said. Fiesp's latest economic forecast, however, points to growth of about four percent, he said.

Piva added that industrial firings could increase at a faster pace if the government moves to slow down the economy in a bid to curb a mounting trade deficit, expected to hit $7 billion or $8 billion in 1997.
